annotations.title: List the clients waiting on a decision

description: Returns who has been fetching this site and what the owner has already decided about them — the review queue first. A queue row is a client the site wants a verdict on: brand new, unusually heavy, or caught claiming an identity that is not its own. A client the owner already blocked is handled and never listed here, so `reviewTotal` is the same count the owner’s own bell shows. `flags` says why a row is queued and `severity` how loud; `hits` is every request under the row’s name — on a row whose verdict is spoofed, read `spoofHits`/`spoofLastSeen` for the impostor’s own volume and recency, because the genuine engine can share the exact same user-agent string and `verifiedHits` of those requests proved to be really it. `suggestedRule` is the exact user-agent fragment a block or allow would match on — pass it nothing, pass review-client the `ua`. Then the standing decisions: `blocked` (turned away at the door), `allowed` (never blocked, never queued again) and `ignored` (a not-now, no policy either way, which returns if the client changes materially). `verifiers` is the separate list of crawlers whose identity CAN be proved by reverse DNS or published IP ranges — recheck-client only works on those. Empty queue plus enabled=true means nothing needs a verdict; enabled=false means the site is not recording visits at all, which is not the same as nobody visiting.
name: agentimus-read-clients

decidedAt.description: Unix time the owner decided; 0 = the record predates the decision log.
Unix time the owner decided; 0 = the record predates the decision log.

enabled.description: Whether this site records machine visits at all. False = the lists below are silence, not evidence.

identifyOn.description: Whether "identify every bot" is on, which is what fills in the owning network.

hits.description: The volume the owner saw when they ignored it — the row returns if the client grows well past this.

key.description: Send this as `ua` to review-client with decision=forget and list=ignored to undo it.

name.description: The client that was set aside, as the owner sees it named.

hits.description: Every request under this row’s name, verified and failing alike — on a spoofed row, `spoofHits` is the impostor’s own share.

ips.description: The captured source addresses behind this row — what a host/CDN block would target; the owner’s Details drawer shows the same list. Filled only when the owner stores IPs for flagged clients: empty means "not captured", never "no address".

isHeavy.description: Fetching far more than the rest.

isNew.description: First seen recently. Leaves the queue on its own if nothing else is wrong.

isSpoof.description: Claimed an identity the identity check disproved — the one flag that never ages out.

lastSeen.description: ISO 8601 — the newest request under this name, whoever sent it. On a spoofed row the impostor’s own recency is `spoofLastSeen`.

name.description: What it is, when this site recognises it; empty when nothing does.

recentHits.description: How many of those are recent — the burst that raised it.

refused.description: Whether requests from it are already being turned away at the door.

severity.description: How loud the row is; higher wants attention sooner.

spoofHits.description: Requests that FAILED the identity check — the impostor’s own volume. Never read `hits` as the impostor’s: the genuine engine can share this exact name.

spoofLastSeen.description: ISO 8601 — when the last FAILING request was seen: the date the spoofed verdict rests on. Can be far older than `lastSeen`. Empty when the verdict came from an admin re-check rather than logged requests.

suggestedRule.description: The user-agent fragment a block or allow would match on. Empty means no safe rule can be derived, and review-client will refuse block and allow for this row.

ua.description: The client’s user-agent, as sent. Pass this to review-client and recheck-client.

verdict.description: What the identity check makes of it: unchecked, verified or spoofed.

verifiable.description: Whether its claimed identity CAN be proved — recheck-client only works on these.

verifiedHits.description: Requests under this same name that forward-confirmed as the genuine engine. Non-zero on a spoofed row means the real engine also visits — only the failing requests are the impostor.

reviewTotal.description: Rows in the queue — the same count the owner’s bell shows (already-blocked clients are handled, not queued).

domains.description: The hostnames a genuine one resolves to.

ua.description: The user-agent fragment that claims this identity.
